title: Superwhisper vs Wispr Flow on Mac in 2026: price, offline dictation and platforms
metaTitle: Superwhisper vs Wispr Flow on Mac: offline, price, platforms
description: Superwhisper vs Wispr Flow on Mac: offline dictation, privacy, platforms and prices from each company's own site. Lazur is a third option.
intro: Superwhisper can transcribe offline, but only with on-device models, and those run best on Apple silicon Macs. Wispr Flow always transcribes in the cloud, so it needs internet. This page compares price, privacy and platforms using each company's own site, and reviews are labeled as opinion.
tldr: Superwhisper can run on-device models offline, best on Apple silicon Macs.
Wispr Flow transcribes in the cloud only, according to its own data-controls page.
Wispr Flow Pro is $15/user/mo monthly or $12/user/mo annual. Superwhisper's Pro price is not confirmed, so check its site.
Superwhisper lists Mac, Windows, iOS, Android and Linux. Wispr Flow lists Mac, Windows, iPhone and Android.
Lazur is a Mac-only third option that sees your screen and answers out loud.

blocks.text: Price: what each company shows on its own site

Start with price, since it is the first thing most people compare. Wispr Flow's pricing page lists Free at $0 and Pro at $15/user/mo monthly or $12/user/mo annual. It also lists Growth and Enterprise. The page does not label which of its two Growth prices applies to which billing period.

Superwhisper is harder to pin down. Its homepage shows Free at $0 and Pro as '$849', with no billing period next to it. The page has Monthly, Yearly and Lifetime toggles, but it prints no Pro price for yearly or lifetime. Its dedicated pricing URL returned a 404 when checked on 2026-11-07.

So this page does not give a Superwhisper Pro price. Some review sites and search snippets list other figures. Those were not confirmed on Superwhisper's own site, so do not use them to decide. See their pricing page before you buy, or check the price inside the app's account screen.

items: Open https://superwhisper.com and scroll to the plan cards.
Switch between Monthly, Yearly and Lifetime and note what each option shows.
If the Pro price still has no billing period, do not guess. Contact Superwhisper through its site before you pay.
Keep the refund rule in mind. The homepage states a 30-day refund for all plans.

blocks.text: To compare a year of Wispr Flow, multiply the rate by 12 yourself. Pro billed monthly uses the $15 rate. Pro billed annually uses the $12 rate. Check the pricing page for billing rules before you pick a cycle, because the page lists rates per user.

Lazur uses a different model. It has a 3-day Pro trial with no credit card, and the trial starts the first time you open the app. Pro is $18/month, or $15/month billed annually, with 150 AI actions. Power is $120/month, or $96/month billed annually, with 1,000 AI actions. Dictation is unlimited on both plans.

A common mistake is comparing a Superwhisper figure from a review site with Wispr's official Pro price. Compare only the prices you confirmed on each company's own page, and write down the date you checked.
Offline dictation: what works without internet

This is where the two apps differ most. Superwhisper says it works offline, so you can transcribe anytime. Its privacy policy says that when you use a local model, your audio and transcripts never leave your device. That is the real offline mode.

Offline use has limits, and Superwhisper says so on its homepage. Intel Macs work best with cloud models. Offline models only run really well on Apple Silicon Macs. If your Mac has an Intel chip, expect to rely on cloud models for most dictation.

A tldv reviewer says only two on-device models work offline. The reviewer calls the offline promise real but narrower than the marketing suggests. Superwhisper's homepage does not name those two models. Treat this as one reviewer's opinion, and check the model list in the app.

Wispr Flow works the other way. Its data-controls page says, 'Transcription always occurs on the cloud.' A tldv reviewer also reports no offline mode, which is opinion. Wispr's own wording is the stronger source. With no network, Wispr Flow has no way to transcribe.

items: Pick an on-device model in Superwhisper, not a cloud model.
Turn Wi-Fi off from Apple menu > System Settings > Wi-Fi.
Hold your dictation shortcut and say a test sentence with a name and a number in it.
Compare the text with what you said. Note any missed names or numbers.
Turn Wi-Fi back on and repeat the test with a cloud model. The difference shows what you gain offline.

blocks.text: The usual mistake is testing with Wi-Fi still on. A cloud model answers over the network, so the test proves nothing. Turn Wi-Fi off first, then dictate.

Take a train ride with no signal. Superwhisper with an on-device model on an Apple silicon Mac can still type your notes. Wispr Flow cannot. That is the clearest difference on this page, so it should drive your choice if offline use matters to you.
Privacy: where your audio goes

The two companies handle AI training differently. Superwhisper's privacy policy, last updated October 8, 2026, says its cloud models do not use your data for training. Wispr says training applies only if you opt in to share your content.

With a cloud model, your audio, transcript and any prompt or context are sent for processing. Superwhisper says audio and transcripts processed by its cloud models are not stored on its servers after the request completes. Its server logs are kept for 30 days. Crash and error reports can be kept for up to 90 days.

If you bring your own API key, the app sends requests straight to that provider. Superwhisper says it does not see that content. That gives you more control, but your privacy then depends on the AI provider you chose.

Wispr Flow's data-controls page is thinner on dictation detail. It says transcription always occurs on the cloud. Its Dictation Cloud Storage setting controls whether Wispr stores your transcription data. Data is encrypted in transit and at rest. The page does not state defaults, and it does not say how long dictation audio is kept.

Wispr's privacy policy says AI subprocessor content is generally deleted within 30 days, subject to each provider's retention practices. A tldv reviewer says the 'Improve the model for everyone' setting is on by default on Free and Pro. Wispr's pages do not state that default, so check the setting in the app before you dictate client material.

Wispr also lists SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001 and HIPAA on its homepage. Superwhisper lists SOC 2 Type II under its Enterprise plan. A certificate covers a specific audit scope, so read what it covers before you buy for a team.

Lazur's stance is simpler. It listens and looks at your screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer you, and they are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models.
Platforms: Mac, Windows, iPhone, Android and Linux

Superwhisper covers the most platforms here. Its homepage lists macOS, Windows, iOS, Android and Linux. The Meetings feature on its Free plan is Mac only. Its latest changelog entry is version 3.2.1, dated November 6, 2026, but the page does not say which platform it applies to.

Wispr Flow lists Mac, Windows, iPhone and Android. Its Notetaker runs on Windows and Mac only, so meeting notes do not reach phones. If your team mixes Macs with Windows PCs, both apps list Windows, but only Superwhisper also lists Linux.
Lazur runs on macOS only, on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, not available. If you need one tool on a Windows PC, Lazur is not the answer today.

Superwhisper's App Store listing shows version 3.2, for iPhone only, and requires iOS 26.0 or later. It shows an average rating of 4.4 from 859 ratings. App Store version numbers may not match the Mac build, so check the version inside your own app.
Do not assume features match across platforms. Meetings is Mac only on Superwhisper's Free plan. Notetaker is not on phones for Wispr. Check each feature on each device you use.
Accuracy and cleanup: what reviewers say

Neither company gave a verified accuracy score that this page could use. Wispr's own accuracy claims were not confirmed on its pages, so this page leaves them out. The reviews below are opinions from a third-party blog, and they are labeled that way.

A tldv reviewer measured Superwhisper at about 98% accuracy on plain everyday text. The same reviewer found weak spots. Proper nouns were unreliable. Numbers sometimes changed between runs. Cleanup sometimes altered the meaning of a sentence.

For Wispr Flow, the same reviewer praised context-aware tone, filler-word removal and cross-device sync. The review also criticized reports of quality drift, Notetaker slowing an 8 GB Mac, and an experimental Command Mode.

Why does this matter? Speech is fast, but errors cost time. A 2016 preprint on touchscreen phones found speech entry about 2.9 times faster than a keyboard, at 153 words per minute against 52. Speech had a lower corrected error rate, 5.30% against 11.22%. It left more uncorrected errors, 1.30% against 0.79%.

So plan for a review pass. Read names, numbers and dates before you send anything. Use the [dictation accuracy checker](/tools/dictation-accuracy-checker) to test your own voice and microphone. Use the [speaking vs typing test](/tools/speaking-vs-typing-test) to see how much faster speech is for you.
The common mistake is trusting a clean-looking paragraph. Cleanup can smooth a sentence and change what it says.
Meeting notes: Superwhisper Meetings and Wispr Notetaker

Both apps offer a meeting feature, and they work differently. Superwhisper's Meetings is on the Free plan and is Mac only. Wispr Flow's Notetaker runs on Mac and Windows only, and its free access is limited.

Wispr's Notetaker privacy overview says uploaded meeting audio is deleted 7 days after upload. If a meeting never finishes processing, its local audio is kept for 30 days instead. Model training is always off on Growth and Enterprise plans, and when a HIPAA Business Associate Agreement is signed.

Wispr also says Notetaker launched after its SOC 2 and ISO/IEC 27001 audit periods and was not assessed in them. If a certificate matters to your work, ask for the current audit scope before you record a client call.
Where Lazur fits as a third option

Lazur is a different kind of tool. It is a voice assistant that lives in the Mac notch. Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask about anything on screen, and Lazur answers out loud. Hold fn to dictate clean, formatted text at the cursor in any app.

Use it when the problem sits on your screen. Ask where something is, and Lazur draws a circle and a label around it. Ask how to do something, and Lazur guides you one click at a time, waiting for each click. For a new app, ask Lazur to walk you through it. Lazur does not click buttons or operate other apps for you.
Dictation comes with Lazur, but it is not the headline. You get snippets, a personal dictionary and clipboard slots. Dictation is unlimited on both the Pro and Power plans.
Lazur's product facts do not list an offline mode. If offline dictation is your main need, Superwhisper is the better fit. Lazur is also Mac only, with no Windows or phone app.
Mistakes people make when they compare these two

items: Comparing a Superwhisper price from a review site with Wispr's official Pro price. Check both on the company's own page.
Testing offline mode with Wi-Fi on. The cloud model answers, so the test tells you nothing.
Expecting offline dictation on an Intel Mac. Superwhisper says offline models run really well only on Apple Silicon.
Assuming Wispr Flow works offline. Its data-controls page says transcription always occurs on the cloud.
Leaving Wispr's training setting unchecked. Check it before you dictate anything sensitive.
Going past Wispr's Free limit without noticing. The homepage caps Free at 2,000 words per week.

blocks.text: Which one to pick
Pick Superwhisper if

items: Offline dictation on an Apple silicon Mac is the main requirement.
You want to bring your own AI API keys.
You need Linux along with Mac and Windows.

blocks.text: Pick Wispr Flow if

items: Cloud dictation is fine and you need Windows or a phone too.
You want meeting notes on Mac or Windows, with the retention rules above.
A Free plan capped at 2,000 words per week suits your use.

blocks.text: Pick Lazur if

items: You want help with what is on your screen, not only typing.
You learn new Mac apps often and want a guide that waits for each click.
You want dictation and an assistant in one Mac app.

blocks.text: Some people run two tools, one for long dictation and one for on-screen help. That is a valid setup. Keep the app you trust most with sensitive work, and check its data controls first.
What to do next

items: Confirm Superwhisper's current Pro price on its site before you choose. Do not rely on a figure with no billing period.
Run the offline test above on your own Mac, with Wi-Fi off.
If you try Wispr Flow's Free plan, count your words for a week against the 2,000 words per week limit.
Read the privacy and data-controls pages for the app you pick, then set its storage and training options.
For more options, read [Wispr Flow alternatives for Mac](/alternatives/wispr-flow) or [Superwhisper alternatives for Mac](/alternatives/superwhisper).

faq.question: Is Superwhisper cheaper than Wispr Flow?
faq.answer: Not confirmed yet. Wispr Flow's pricing page lists Pro at $15/user/mo monthly or $12/user/mo annual. Superwhisper's homepage shows '$849' with no billing period, and its pricing URL returned a 404 when checked on 2026-11-07. Check Superwhisper's current price on its site before you decide.

faq.question: Does Wispr Flow work offline?
faq.answer: No, according to its own site. Wispr's data-controls page says transcription always occurs on the cloud. A tldv reviewer also reports no offline mode, which is opinion. With no network, Wispr Flow cannot transcribe.

faq.question: Does Superwhisper work offline on an Intel Mac?
faq.answer: It can, but with cloud models. Superwhisper says Intel Macs work best with cloud models, and offline models only run really well on Apple Silicon Macs. Test an on-device model on your own Mac with Wi-Fi off before you rely on it.

faq.question: Does every Superwhisper model work offline?
faq.answer: Not according to one reviewer. A tldv reviewer says only two on-device models work offline, and Superwhisper's homepage does not name them. Check the model list inside the app before you plan around it.

faq.question: Does Lazur run on Windows?
faq.answer: No. Lazur runs on macOS, on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, not available.

faq.question: Does Wispr Flow use my dictation to train its AI?
faq.answer: Wispr says model training applies only if you opt in to share your content. A tldv reviewer says the 'Improve the model for everyone' setting is on by default on Free and Pro. Wispr's pages do not state that default, so check it in the app.

faq.question: How long does Wispr keep meeting audio?
faq.answer: Its Notetaker privacy overview says uploaded meeting audio is deleted 7 days after upload. If a meeting never finishes processing, its local audio is kept for 30 days instead.

faq.question: Can I try Lazur before I pay?
faq.answer: Yes. Lazur has a 3-day Pro trial with no credit card. The trial starts the first time you open the app, so open it when you are ready to test.
